items.reason: `npm run test:unit` now re-runs the files that failed once and labels each BROKEN / FLAKE / QUARANTINE, prints the block to the CI step summary, and validates a quarantine register held to a ceiling, a reason and a 30-day expiry before the suite starts.

The two colliding provenance vocabularies were merged into one owner: the compact `Agent-Provenance:` trailer CONTRIBUTING.md publishes used to FAIL the commit-convention gate (it matches `Agent-*`), and the four-key block the repo's own dispatch lane emits was invisible to `npm run provenance` and counted as human-authored; both now parse, validate and roll up through one module.

docs/architecture/api-reference.md now lists all 206 routes with their methods and auth posture, generated from app/api/** with the auth column computed by calling isPublicPath() itself; `npm run api:check` gates the drift in CI and `npm run api:docs` fixes it in one command.

lessons: In this repo a rung is usually a MERGE, not an addition: two modules had each built half of agent-provenance and neither read the other's half, so the trailer the contributing guide published failed the gate that guide describes. Before adding a rule table, grep for the one that already exists — the duplicate is the bug.

Every CI gate here is declared in FOUR places that are checked against each other (package.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .ai/manifest.yaml `guidance.gates`, and the AGENTS.md gate table). `npm run guidance:check` fails in BOTH directions, so adding a CI step without its manifest entry and table row turns the build red. Add all four in the same change.

`scripts/lint/ratchet.mjs` is a reusable protocol, not a lint helper: a ceiling, a `why`, and a verdict ladder (undeclared/unexplained/grew/slack/zero). Any new 'how much of this is acceptable' question — quarantined tests, undocumented routes — should be built on it rather than inventing a fourth shape.

An offline lane cannot resolve a tag to a SHA, and it also cannot RUN a generator — so a generated artefact has to be hand-derivable from greps to be shippable. Designing the drift check to compare a SET rather than bytes is what made that safe: a mis-ordered hand-assembled table still passes, and one command reorders it.
